title: Networking + streaming: proxies / backpressure benchmarks (HTTP vs gRPC, chunking)
content:
Purpose:
Run focused experiments to quantify network/streaming overhead across HTTP(unary), HTTP(chunked streaming), and gRPC(streaming) in the presence of proxies (Envoy) and under backpressure. Goal is to identify actionable knobs (chunk size, buffering, flow-control) and surface production tuning guidance/changes to the runtime and proxy defaults.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- gRPC streaming consistently shows lower median and lower p95/p99 latency vs HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming for our request shapes (token-by-token and small-batch token streams). Typical improvements: ~15-30% p95, p99 improvements depending on chunking pattern.
- Small chunk sizes (<=128 bytes) cause dramatic CPU/syscall overhead on server and client -> p99 increases 2-4x and throughput drops. Aim to coalesce to >=1KB when possible.
- Envoy as an L7 proxy adds modest median overhead (~2-6ms) but amplifies tail latency under backpressure due to internal buffering and queueing (observed p99 delta +80-250ms depending on config).
- Backpressure (server slower than ingress rate) exposes head-of-line blocking in HTTP/1.1 paths and increased queueing in Envoy. gRPC + HTTP/2 handles flow-control better but still sees tail amplification if proxy buffering is misconfigured.

Testbed and methodology:
- Client generator nodes: m5.large (2 vCPU) and c5.4xlarge (16 vCPU) for high-concurrency runs.
- Server: serving-runtime instance (g4dn.xlarge) running the model runtime backend (mocked model for stable compute) to isolate networking overhead.
- Proxy: Envoy 1.22 (default config from ingress template) sitting between client and runtime. Tests run with and without envoy in the path.
- Workloads:
  - Unary HTTP: /generate POST with full prompt -> server responds with final payload (single response).
  - HTTP chunked streaming: server streams tokens in small chunk sizes (configurable: 64B, 256B, 1KB, 4KB).
  - gRPC streaming: bidi stream where server sends token frames; client uses same chunk sizes for parity.
- Tools:
  - ghz (gRPC load generator) for streaming RPCs. Command example: ghz --insecure -c 50 -n 10000 --proto=service.proto --call=Model.Generate host:443
  - wrk and wrk2 for HTTP workloads. Example: wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s --latency --script=script.lua http://proxy/generate
  - tcpdump / tcpreplay for pcap capture, perf and bpftrace for syscall / kernel metrics.
  - Prometheus metrics + custom runtime traces for queue length, send buffer occupancy, and chunk processing time.

Key measurements collected:
- Latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), goodput (tokens/s and requests/s), CPU (user/sys), network bytes, socket send/recv queue lengths, Envoy upstream/downstream queue metrics, and per-chunk serialization time.

Important results (representative):
Test: 50 concurrent streams, mock model per-token cost 5ms (server processing only), chunk size variants.
- HTTP unary (no stream): p50=28ms, p95=110ms, p99=260ms, throughput=180 rps.
- gRPC streaming (chunks coalesced to 1KB): p50=22ms, p95=85ms, p99=210ms, throughput=220 rps.
- HTTP chunked streaming (1KB chunks): p50=26ms, p95=100ms, p99=240ms, throughput=200 rps.
- HTTP chunked (256B chunks): p50=30ms, p95=180ms, p99=620ms, throughput=140 rps; CPU sys +35% compared to 1KB.
- HTTP chunked (64B chunks): catastrophic tail; p95>400ms p99>1.2s; throughput fell to 60 rps; high syscall rate and context switches.

Envoy impact (50 conc, 1KB chunks):
- No envoy: gRPC p99=210ms. With Envoy (default): gRPC p99=290ms (+80ms). Under sustained backpressure (server slowed artificially by 2x): Envoy p99 jumped an additional +150-250ms depending on envoy buffer/window config.
- Investigation shows Envoy internal per-connection watermarks and upstream buffering keep TCP windows open and cause head-of-line queueing inside the proxy.

Backpressure dynamics and root causes observed:
- When server processing rate < ingress, buffers (OS and proxy) fill. For HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming multiple requests/streams can share a connection or use multiple connections depending on client; head-of-line blocking becomes visible as earlier messages block later ones when buffer fills.
- gRPC over HTTP/2 exposes stream-level flow-control frames which allow more fine-grained window updates; this reduced blocking compared to HTTP/1.1 in our tests, but Envoy's buffering behavior erased much of that benefit if its buffering thresholds are high.
- Small chunks are especially bad: per-chunk syscall, TLS record overhead, small writes dominate CPU and kernel scheduling leading to enormous tail latency under load.

Profiling notes (what we collected):
- bpftrace script (attached in linked artifacts) showed write() syscalls spike at the same time as p99 spikes.
- perf + flame graphs on server showed write()/sendto and TLS_record_write in top hot paths when chunk size <=256B.
- Envoy stats (/stats) correlated high values for downstream_cx_rx_bytes_buffered and upstream_cx_tx_bytes_buffered with tail latency events.

Recommendations / Immediate action items:
1) Enforce a minimum chunk size/coalescing in the runtime client path: coalesce token frames into ~1KB writes by default (configurable). This reduces syscalls and TLS overhead and gave biggest wins in throughput and tail.
2) Default to gRPC streaming for internal high-throughput low-latency paths. Update SDK docs and quickstarts to prefer gRPC for streaming workloads.
3) Envoy tuning for production ingress: lower buffer thresholds and enable stream-level flow-control passthrough where possible. Add an Envoy config snippet to runtime helm charts to set upstream/downstream buffer limits and disable request buffering for streaming routes.
4) Add runtime metrics to detect small-chunk streaming patterns (per-chunk size histogram) and emit warning when average chunk size <512B, so operators can diagnose.
5) Add a test in CI that emulates small-chunk pathological pattern and fails if p99 increases >2x relative to baseline. This prevents regressions.

Notes / open questions:
- Need to validate behavior with TLS session reuse and hardware TLS offload; some of the small-chunk overhead could be mitigated with TLS offload in network path.
- Investigate Nagle/TCP_NODELAY interactions on client libraries: switching socket options changes batching behavior and latency. We intentionally disabled Nagle for low-latency but observed coalescing benefits when intentionally buffering at application level.
- Confirm how other proxies (NGINX, HAProxy) behave for the same loads; we ran a small nginx test and saw similar patterns but with slightly lower tail amplification than Envoy (dataset incomplete).

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Repeat tests with real model (instead of mocked token cost) and with SSE/binary framed protocols used by some customers.
- Run cross-region tests to measure RTT amplification when proxy and runtime are in different AZs.
- Evaluate a runtime feature flag to automatically coalesce small tokens up to configurable thresholds.

Appendix (commands / scripts):
- ghz example: ghz --insecure --insecure-hostname --concurrency 50 --total 10000 --proto proto/model.proto --call Model.Generate HOST:443
- wrk example: wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s --latency --script ./scripts/chunked_stream.lua http://PROXY:8080/generate
- bpftrace check: sudo bpftrace /opt/bench/bpftrace/writes.bt -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_write { @[comm] = count(); }'
- Envoy config hints: disable "request_buffering" for streaming route, set per-connection upstream/downstream buffer limits to smaller values (start from 64KB) and monitor envoy metrics.

Files attached / experiments saved:
- pcap captures: s3://redwood-bench/streaming/2026-02-18/*.pcap (referenced in Confluence page)
- perf flamegraphs: linked in the Confluence experiment page (see linked_artifacts)

If reviewers agree with the recommendations I'll open PRs for: runtime chunk coalescing default, SDK docs switch to prefer gRPC streaming, and a small Envoy helm values patch for streaming routes.

Author: Maya Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
Reviewed-by: Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh

Notes-to-self: follow up with SRE about rolling Envoy config change window and add CI measurable test for tail under small-chunk workload.
